title: The Position of a Permutation in the Dictionary

concept.title: Count the permutations that come before, without listing them
body: List all permutations of `1 .. n` in dictionary order. What is the **rank** of a given permutation `p` (the first permutation is rank 1)? Listing them is hopeless for `n = 20` (more than 2 * 10^18 permutations), but they can be **counted** in blocks. Look at the first position: every permutation that starts with a smaller value than `p[0]` comes before `p`, and for each such starting value there are exactly `(n - 1)!` permutations. Then the same question is asked for the rest.

Only the values that are **not used yet** can stand at position `i`, so `smaller` counts only those. The answer is one more than the number of permutations before `p`. This is the same idea as skipping whole branches in a search, but we do not walk the branches: we **count** them with a factorial and jump over them.

statement: All permutations of the numbers `1, 2, ..., n` are written in dictionary order (compare the first numbers, then the second numbers, and so on). The first one is `1 2 ... n`. Given a permutation, print its position in this list (starting at 1).
inputFormat: The second line has the permutation.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 20 (20! is about 2.4 * 10^18 and fits in a 64-bit integer)
The second line is a permutation of 1 to n.
hints: Permutations that start with a smaller number all come before; there are (n - 1)! of them for each smaller number.
Count only the smaller numbers that are not used yet.
Repeat for the next position with one number less, and add one at the end because the ranks start at 1.

starter.python:
n = int(input())
p = list(map(int, input().split()))

# Your code here

explanation: At position `i`, every unused value smaller than `p[i]` starts `(n - 1 - i)!` permutations that come earlier. The function adds these blocks and continues with the next position; the final answer is one more than the count of earlier permutations.
